04

About & teaching

I am an associate professor in the Department of Information Management at Hacettepe University, Türkiye. I received my bachelor’s degree in statistics and my master’s and doctoral degrees in information management from Hacettepe University.

My research focuses on research evaluation, bibliometrics and scholarly communication. My interests include university rankings, responsible research assessment, the evaluation of the social sciences and humanities, open science, research data management, bibliographic data quality and research integrity.

My master’s research mapped the intellectual structure of library and information science literature in Türkiye. My doctoral research evaluated international university ranking systems using their overall rankings and indicators.

I led a TÜBİTAK-funded postdoctoral project on university rankings and responsible research assessment (2022–2024). I have contributed to national and international projects on open access policies, library services, research assessment and questionable publishing, and I am a researcher on OPENRAM (Opening Research Assessment to Multi-Contexts).

I teach courses in research methods, bibliometrics, social network analysis and scholarly communication, and supervise graduate research. I serve on the FORCE11 Board of Directors, the ASIS&T Professional Development Committee and the editorial board of the Annual Review of Information Science and Technology (ARIST). I also take part in collaborative open peer review through the FORCE11 PREreview Club.
